To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antimicrobial activity is highly dependent on the chemical composition and the structural features of the copolymers immobilized on polymeric films.
the antimicrobial activity depends on the chemical and structural characteristics of the copolymers and the immobilization of the active polymers on the surface.

the antimicrobial efficiency of cationic copolymers is strongly dependent on the structure of the polymer and that the best antimicrobial efficiency is achieved with copolymers containing quaternized groups with a high positive charge density in combination with a flexible structure.

the development of novel antimicrobial polymers and surfaces, and the study of their structure-activity relationship.
the development of novel antimicrobial surfaces based on cationic copolymers.
the design, synthesis and characterization of novel copolymers and the development of efficient antimicrobial films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria is strongly influenced by the hydrophilicity and flexibility of the side chain of the copolymers, whereas for the Gram-positive bacteria, the hydrophilicity of the side chain and the charge density of the quaternary ammoniun groups are the most important parameters for the activity.
the best antimicrobial films can be prepared by blending copolmers with high charge density and good chain mobility.
the best results were obtained with copolymers containing quaternary ammonio groups in the main chain and a high degree of chain flexibility.

the chemical composition and the structure of the copolymers are the key factors for obtaining efficient antimicrobial surfaces.
the antimicrobial efficiency is related to the chemical structure of the polymer, which determines the flexibility of the side chain and the positive charge density.
the antimicrobial activity depends on the structure of the polymer, the nature of the microorganism, and the environmental conditions (pH, ionic strength, temperature, etc.).

it is possible to tailor the macromolecular structure of cationic polymers to achieve efficient contact active antimicrobial surfaces.
the antimicrobial activity is strongly dependent on the macromolecular structure of the copolymer and that the design of these polymers can be tuned to achieve the desired antimicrobial properties.
